summary.text: The Knights Templar were a Catholic military order founded in 1118 to defend pilgrims on their way to Jerusalem, with their headquarters on the Temple Mount.
Endorsed by the Church, they became a favoured charity across Christendom, and their knights in white mantles with a red cross were among the most skilled fighting units of the Crusades.
As much as 90% of members were non-combatants who managed a large economic infrastructure, and Pope Clement V disbanded the order in 1312.

facts.label: Founded
facts.value: 1118, to defend pilgrims travelling to Jerusalem

facts.value: Two knights on one horse, showing poverty

facts.value: As much as 90% of the order's members

items.prompt: An early Templar seal showed two knights riding a single horse. What did the order want it to stress?

options.label: Its poverty
Its speed in battle
Its loyalty to the king
Its noble birth

items.explain: The order had few financial resources, and its emblem of two knights on a single horse emphasised its poverty.

items.prompt: A pilgrim leaves valuables with a local Templar house, takes a document, and collects equal treasure on arrival in the Holy Land. What was this arrangement?

options.label: A tax that pilgrims paid to the king
An early form of banking that protected pilgrims from robbery
A ransom scheme for captured pilgrims
A way to pay the order's soldiers' wages

items.explain: Letters of credit were an early form of banking that protected pilgrims from robbery while adding to Templar finances.

items.prompt: Each Templar was sworn to poverty, yet the order itself held vast wealth. What explains this?

options.label: Individual members kept private fortunes in secret
The pope paid the order a large yearly salary
Donations and business dealings built financial networks across Christendom
The order lived off treasure won in raids alone

items.explain: Although individual members were sworn to poverty, a mix of donations and business dealings let the order establish financial networks across Christendom.

items.prompt: In 1307 a French king had many Templars in France arrested. How did the order finally end?

options.label: Pope Clement V disbanded it in 1312 under pressure from the king
It merged with the Hospitallers and kept its lands
It was defeated in battle by Saladin's army
It disbanded itself once its mission was done

items.explain: Under pressure from King Philip IV, Pope Clement V disbanded the order in 1312.

items.prompt: A 1139 papal bull exempted the Templars from obedience to local laws. What did that mean for them?

options.label: They paid taxes only to the kings of Europe
They answered to the Patriarch of Jerusalem alone
They had to follow the laws of each kingdom
They were free of taxes and answered to no authority but the pope

items.explain: The bull meant the Templars could pass freely through all borders, were not required to pay taxes, and were exempt from all authority except that of the pope.

items.prompt: A visitor expects every Templar to be a knight charging into battle. How would a historian correct him?

options.label: Only the nobles in the order ever held any weapons
Most members were in support roles, not fighting
All members fought, but only on foot
Fighting was forbidden to the order's members

items.explain: Although the primary mission of the order was military, relatively few members were combatants, and the majority acted in support positions.
